en.t: Bai Juyi, in Hearing the Night Pestle, wrote:

units.source_text: “谁家思妇秋捣帛，月苦风凄砧杵悲。

en.t: Whose longing wife is pounding silk in autumn? The moon is harsh, the wind is cold, and the block and pestle sound mournful.

units.source_text: 八月九月正长夜，千声万声无了时。

en.t: In the eighth and ninth months, when the nights are at their longest, the thousand and ten thousand blows seem never to end.

units.source_text: 应到天明头尽白，一声添得一茎丝。”

en.t: By dawn her hair must have turned completely white; with every sound, one more strand of white hair is added.
